one_month_reasoning: No scheduled company catalyst falls inside 2026-10-03 to 2026-11-01: Q3 2026 results are expected around Nov 3-5 (source 27), just after the window (Q2 was reported Aug 4). Possible but unscheduled: an RPO/deal pre-announcement like the July 7 one (source 26), insider 10b5-1 sales continuing (sources 3-5; mild supply, not news), and macro/AI-capex sentiment swings that have driven 7-9% single-day moves without company news (sources 2,3). The stock is ~25% off its June high after a +290% year, so neither momentum nor reversal gives a strong signal. I therefore center the 1-month distribution on today's price with a tiny negative log drift and use monthly sigma = 82%/3.5 = 23.4%, giving P(>=140.07)=0.49.

bear.story: AI-native demand proves lumpy/concentrated: one or two nine-figure customers slip or renegotiate, 2027 growth lands in the 30s not >50%, while $2.8B of lease commitments and GPU depreciation hit COGS ahead of revenue. GAAP EPS stays negative, FCF margin compresses, and the market re-rates DOCN toward neocloud/DC multiples (~12-13x NTM EBITDA of ~$850M) -> ~$75, roughly the March offering price.

base.story: Growth accelerates to ~45-50% in 2027 as guided but decelerates into 2028; EBITDA margin ~38-40%; multiple compresses from ~26x to ~20x NTM EBITDA as the mix becomes more capital-intensive. Earnings growth roughly offsets multiple compression -> stock roughly flat to slightly down.

bull.story: More nine-figure inference contracts, RPO compounds, 2027 growth >50% with stable margins; market keeps paying a software-like ~28-30x on ~$1.1B NTM EBITDA -> ~$230.

comps_summary.peer_range: Basis: MarketScreener consensus for fiscal 2027 (= calendar 2027; all 11 peers and DOCN have December year ends), one source and one date. EV/EBITDA CY2027: 7.5x (CRWV) to 128x (NET), median 20.3x. P/E CY2027 on MarketScreener's (GAAP-like) EPS: 23x (GOOGL) to 5,050x (NET), median 61.0x over the 8 peers with positive EPS (FSLY, CRWV, NBIS loss-making, recorded as null). EV/sales CY2027 median 6.67x (2.9x-33x).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: DOCN trades at 25.9x CY2027 EV/EBITDA and 10.4x EV/sales today (source 11), above the peer medians; its CY2027 GAAP EPS consensus on the same basis is negative (-$0.08), so P/E is not meaningful on this basis (on company non-GAAP EPS ~$1.70 for 2027 it is ~82x). We apply 20.0x EV/EBITDA (at the median) and 7.5x EV/sales (just above median, inside range) to CY2028 numbers.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium to the median is applied. Growth is higher than most peers, but it is being bought with leased data-center capacity and debt-financed GPUs (GM fell 60%->55%, $2.8B uncommenced leases, $725M equipment facility), i.e. the economics are converging toward neoclouds (7.5-15x) and DC REITs (20-21x) rather than high-margin software (DDOG 65x, NET 128x). Revenue is increasingly concentrated in a handful of AI-native contracts, which argues against a durable premium. A discount is not imposed either, because DOCN's legacy CPU/SMB cloud business (~80% of ARR) is profitable and sticky.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$85 (about -40%, near the $77 March equity-raise price and the August low area ~$100 broken decisively) the market would be pricing growth well under the 35%+/50% trajectory or a lost/renegotiated nine-figure AI contract, i.e. a fundamental reset of the AI-native thesis (or a financing problem around the leases/equipment facility), not ordinary 82%-vol noise.

reasoning: Skeptic lane. Fundamentals are genuinely strong (Q2-26 revenue +29%, ARR $1.125B, AI ARR +212%, RPO $894M, FY26 guide raised to ~30% growth, >50% targeted for 2027; source 1), so the bear case is about price and quality of growth, not distress. Bear evidence: (i) growth is being bought with capital: GM fell 60%->55%, $2.8B uncommenced DC leases, $578M finance lease/equipment debt, a new $725M (to $1.025B) equipment facility, a March equity raise at $77, and FY26 adj. FCF margin guided down to 11-13% (sources 1,6,7,8,2,25); (ii) Q3 non-GAAP EPS guide ($0.28-0.30) is well below Q2's $0.45, and MarketScreener's CY2027 GAAP EPS consensus is negative (source 11); (iii) insiders sold >$565M with no buying, CEO selling regularly via 10b5-1 (sources 3-5); (iv) concentration in a few AI-native nine-figure contracts (source 26); (v) short interest is modest (~7% of float, falling; source 23) and I found no short-seller report or 2026 downgrade, so the bear case is not crowded. Valuation: on a consistent calendar-2027 basis from one source, DOCN at 25.9x EV/EBITDA sits above the 11-peer median of 20.3x; applying the median to CY2028 EBITDA and a near-median EV/sales gives ~$132, i.e. modestly below the $140 price, versus a sell-side mean target ~$175 (source 9) that I treat as optimistic. Scenarios: bear $75 (30%), base $135 (45%), bull $230 (25%); expectation ~$141, median ~$132. The ladder is a mixture of lognormals around those scenario prices (sigmas 0.25-0.35), giving ~65% annualized spread consistent with, though slightly below, 82% realized vol, and P(>=140)=0.45. Research was limited: Alpha Vantage was rate-limited and Twelve Data estimates required a higher plan, so consensus came from MarketScreener/stockanalysis/tickflow; peer-data sources (11 MarketScreener pages) required by the 10-12 peer rule pull the in-lane share to 11 of 27 overall, while 11 of the 15 non-peer-data sources are in-lane.
